first_impression.reaction: I typed 'crete wedding venues' on the train and the very first sentence splits the island into four areas. That's the answer before I've even scrolled. The takeaways give me the guest-count range, and there's a jump list, so I can skip straight to Chania. I'd read the takeaways, tap one area, glance at the FAQ, then bookmark.

journey.quote: Crete wedding venues sit in four areas: Elounda and Agios Nikolaos in the east, Hersonissos and the Heraklion coast, Rethymno, and Chania and the west.
journey.reaction: First line, straight answer, matches my search word for word. Good start.

journey.quote: Guest count narrows the list fast: Avra Imperial and Elounda Beach publish space for several hundred, while Euphoria's packages are built for up to 30 guests.
journey.reaction: Real names and real numbers in a bullet. This is the one I'd screenshot.
Yes. Four taps and I can skip the overview. Exactly what I want on a phone.

journey.section: Crete wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: The table runs east to west. It is not a ranking.
journey.reaction: Fair enough, and they explain 'Not published' too, which reads honest. But it's six columns and 15 rows, so on my phone I'm swiping sideways to see anything past the venue name.

journey.section: Crete wedding venues at a glance
journey.quote: Your advisor works in your time zone and quotes in AUD.
journey.reaction: AUD? I'm in Singapore. Is this only for Australians?

journey.quote: This is the only venue on the list that is entirely yours for the day, and the only one where every supplier is your choice.
journey.reaction: Ooh. A whole garden to ourselves for 120 people. That's the line that makes me bookmark it.

journey.quote: Not published: room count, exclusive use, curfew.
journey.reaction: Every venue ends with one of these. Honest, but by the third one it feels like the page is listing what it doesn't know.

journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms room counts, ceremony options, exclusive use and curfew in writing for every venue in the west.
journey.reaction: I scrolled up to peek at Elounda and the same line was there too. Feels like a sales loop.

journey.quote: Adults only is a decision, not a detail. If nieces, nephews or godchildren are on the list, this one is out.
journey.reaction: Blunt and useful. I like that it tells me who it's not for.

journey.quote: These terms come from the 2025-2026 brochure, so have them confirmed for a 2027 date.
journey.reaction: Dated. That's exactly what I check for: is this still true?

journey.section: Getting to Crete for your wedding
journey.quote: Booking guests into the wrong airport is the costliest mistake on Crete.
journey.reaction: Didn't know Chania to the east is three hours. Practical, I'd remember that.

journey.quote: Australians entering the Schengen area for a short stay now have fingerprints and a photo taken under the European Entry/Exit System.
journey.reaction: Heading says transfers, first line is about fingerprints at the border for Australians. Not what I tapped for.
A little table with ceremony times by month. Quick and scannable.

journey.quote: Heraklion for the east and centre, Chania for the west.
journey.reaction: Answer in the first five words. Love that.

unanswered_questions: Roughly what does a Crete venue cost? Even a ballpark. Not a single price on the page.
Is this service for people outside Australia, or only Australians?
Which of these can do around 50 to 80 guests? Most venues don't publish a capacity, so I can't tell from the table.

turn_offs_found.quote: Your Wedded Advisor confirms room counts, ceremony options, exclusive use and curfew in writing for every venue in the west.
turn_offs_found.why: A version of this line closes nearly every section (how to compare, Elounda, Agios Nikolaos, the Heraklion coast, Rethymno, the west). Once is helpful; six times feels like being sold to while I'm just trying to read.

turn_offs_found.quote: Australians entering the Schengen area for a short stay now have fingerprints and a photo taken under the European Entry/Exit System.
turn_offs_found.why: It sits under the heading 'Transfers for guests'. When a heading doesn't match what's under it, I stop trusting the headings, and headings are all I read on my phone.

turn_offs_found.quote: Not published: capacity, exclusive use, room count, curfew.
turn_offs_found.why: Fifteen venues each end on a list of what's missing. Skimming, I keep landing on the gaps instead of the good bits.

would_share_with: My cousin who keeps talking about Chania; I'd send her the Chania and the west section and the airport FAQ

cta_reaction.quote: talk to a Wedded Advisor about your shortlist
cta_reaction.why: I'm just looking, not planning yet. No pop-ups and the links don't get in the way, so they didn't annoy me. I'd bookmark before I'd enquire, and the AUD line makes me unsure they'd even work with me.

top_3_changes: Say the 'Your Wedded Advisor confirms...' line once or twice (for example after the comparison section and in the closing), not at the end of every area.

Make the 'Transfers for guests' heading match its content: move the Entry/Exit System paragraph under its own heading (or into the start of 'Getting to Crete') and open the transfers section with the coach and taxi advice.
Lighten the 'Not published' lines (only where it matters most, such as capacity and curfew) so each venue entry ends on what the venue does offer.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Stayed in character as Priya, a casual Google searcher on a phone
No invented brand facts; missing info went to unanswered_questions
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Person-set title, deferred business details and deliberately unprinted prices not treated as must-fix; no request for sourcing lines

assumptions: Persona is provisional (weight 0.10); reactions reflect generic informational search intent.

Arrived from a Google search for 'crete wedding venues' on a phone; read the takeaways, used the jump list to reach Chania and the west, peeked at a few east entries, then the airport, season and FAQ sections.
The '15 Best' title next to 'It is not a ranking' was noticed but not flagged, because the title is person-set and deferred.
Prices are deliberately not printed; the missing ballpark is logged as an unanswered question only.
Read with images not yet loaded; image slots and HTML comments judged as invisible.
Quotes with inline HTML fact comments, link markup or bold markers are given as a reader sees them.
